title: Concept: Non-cryptographic random bytes used as a token in javascript — review required
description: In javascript, crypto.pseudoRandomBytes is called. The Node.js documentation marks the function legacy and states that its output is not cryptographically strong; a token derived from it shrinks the search space an attacker needs when guessing reset links or session identifiers. The call still reads like a crypto API, so reviewers often pass over it.
applicability: javascript services that mint tokens, nonces, or identifiers.
risk: Predictable tokens enabling guessing and account takeover; MEDIUM severity.
